title: Yes/no questions: intonation, est-ce que, inversion
goal: By the end of this lesson you can ask yes/no questions in three registers (intonation, est-ce que, inversion), answer with oui, non and si, and understand the Quebec question particle -tu: Tu viens-tu?

body: The simplest and most common way to ask a yes/no question in speech is to take a normal sentence and make your voice rise at the end: *Tu es prêt?* *Vous parlez anglais?* *Il fait froid?*
The word order does not change at all. In writing, add a question mark (in Quebec usage, no space before it).
learn.tip: Statement: Tu es prêt. ↘  Question: Tu es prêt? ↗

body: Put *est-ce que* (literally 'is it that') at the start of any statement to make it a question. Before a vowel, it becomes *est-ce qu'*: *Est-ce qu'il travaille?*
*Est-ce que* is neutral: fine in conversation, at work and in writing. It sounds like 'ess-kuh'.

head: Statement
Question
rows: Est-ce que vous avez un chien?
Est-ce qu'on peut payer par carte?

body: In formal speech and writing, swap the subject pronoun and the verb and join them with a hyphen: *Vous parlez* → *Parlez-vous?* *Tu es* → *Es-tu?*

If the verb ends in a vowel and the pronoun is *il, elle* or *on*, add *-t-* for sound: *A-t-il un chien? Parle-t-elle français?* With a noun subject, keep the noun and add a pronoun: *Marie est-elle là?* Inversion with *je* is rare; use *est-ce que je…?* instead.
learn.tip: Fixed polite phrases use inversion: Comment allez-vous? Pouvez-vous répéter?

body: Answer *oui* (yes) or *non* (no). But if the question is negative and you want to say 'yes, on the contrary', use *si*: *Tu n'as pas faim? — Si, j'ai faim!* (You're not hungry? — Yes, I am!)
Soften or strengthen your answer: *oui, bien sûr* (yes, of course), *peut-être* (maybe), *non, merci*.

Casual Quebec French has a special yes/no marker: *-tu* placed right after the verb. *Tu viens-tu?* = Are you coming? Here *-tu* is not the pronoun 'you'; it just means 'this is a question'. It works with every subject: *C'est-tu loin?* (Is it far?), *Il vient-tu?* (Is he coming?), *Ça se peut-tu?* (Is that possible?).
It is informal and spoken only, but extremely frequent. Understand it; you can use it with friends once you are comfortable. In writing, use *est-ce que* or intonation.

examples.fr: Est-ce que tu aimes le hockey?
Est-ce qu'on peut payer par carte?

examples.en: Aren't you hungry? — Yes, I am!
Are you coming to the party?

examples.note: Quebec casual: works with any subject

examples.en: Is that possible? / Can you believe it?

quebec.intro: Casual Quebec French marks yes/no questions with -tu after the verb: Tu viens-tu? This -tu isn't 'you'; it's a question particle that works with any subject, as in C'est-tu loin?

items.note: informal; the particle works with c'est

vocab.ex: Il neige en mai? Ça se peut-tu?

pron.tip: Voice rises on the last syllable: prêt ↗.
Quebec: tsu vyan-TSU ↗; the particle is unstressed but the voice rises.

dialogue.fr: Allô! Y'a un party chez Marc samedi. Tu viens-tu?
dialogue.en: Hi! There's a party at Marc's on Saturday. Are you coming?

dialogue.fr: Est-ce que je peux venir avec ma sœur?
dialogue.en: Can I come with my sister?

dialogue.fr: Oui, bien sûr! Elle aime pas la musique forte?
dialogue.en: Yes, of course! Doesn't she like loud music?

speak.model: Tu aimes le café? / Est-ce que tu aimes le café? / Aimes-tu le café?

speak.prompt: Answer the negative question 'Tu n'aimes pas le hockey?' saying that you do like it.

write.prompt: Write 5 polite questions you could ask a new coworker, using est-ce que or inversion.
write.model: Est-ce que vous habitez à Montréal? Parlez-vous anglais? Est-ce que vous aimez le hockey? Avez-vous des enfants? Voulez-vous un café?

quiz.q: The most common way to ask a question in everyday speech is…
quiz.why: Just raise your voice at the end.
-t- between the vowels e and e.

quiz.q: How do you form a question with inversion and a noun subject 'Paul'?
quiz.why: Keep the noun, invert with a pronoun.

options: at the start of the sentence
at the end of any sentence

quiz.q: Is 'Il vient-tu?' possible in Quebec speech?
quiz.why: The particle isn't the pronoun; it marks a question.
